rationale: The FSF executive committee fired Thiaw and his staff on Jul 11 (announced Jul 12). L'Equipe names Vieira as favourite, but Senenews (Jul 12) quotes FSF sources saying he is not the priority and calls Omar Daf the most credible pick on budget grounds. Renard (free since leaving Tunisia Jul 4, lives in Senegal; costly) and Beye are also cited. No decision as of Jul 19.

Japan's crude import volumes fell 64% y/y in April and 57% in May. Nomura puts real crude imports at about 30-40% of the 2025 average in Apr-May (about 90% in June), so Q2 real imports drop sharply vs Q1. Nominal exports rose 15-17% y/y on chips. Net exports should add strongly while inventory drawdown and energy costs weigh on domestic demand (Q1 was already NX +0.3pp vs DD +0.2pp).

STAT (~Jul 10): three finalists (Overton, oncologist Jeffrey Vacirca, DoD health official Stephen Ferrara) were sent to the White House for a final decision, with no nominee as of Jul 16. Food Safety News (Jun 30) says some reports have Ferrara as front-runner; Daily Caller (Jul 9) says Overton is favored. RFK Jr.'s backing for Overton is unclear.
No new information: the Cincinnati draw (event Aug 13-23) comes out around Aug 11. Medvedev lost in Wimbledon R3 to Struff as the 8th seed. Kept a low spread on top players.

Pending SC petitions (Uzma Khan; Imran May 19; early-hearing plea Jun 18) all pray for transfer to Shifa International. The SC returned earlier pleas, and the CJP said the health issue was 'not pending'. All 5 eye injections were given at PIMS (latest Jun 14), the likely middle-path venue. Essentially a coin flip.

Since hostilities resumed (Jul 7-13), Iran has focused on Kuwait and Bahrain. It hit Kuwaiti power and desalination plants (Jul 17-18), and the FT (Jul 21) calls Kuwait Iran's softest target amid rising public anger. The UAE has sought de-escalation and has not been hit. Bahrain's parliament passed a full-boycott proposal in April, and the GCC said (Jun 26) that trade with Iran is 'conditional and reversible'.

Mills has Trump's endorsement, the anti-Mills vote is split, and Florida has no runoff (market about 85-90% Mills, Jun 27). But he raised under $60K in Q2 and has only $81K cash. Elijah won the Seminole Hob Nob straw poll (Jul 9: 45-35-16) and was endorsed by state Sen. Tom Wright (Jul 20). The ethics probe is ongoing.

Kuleba said Ukraine needs wartime elections (Focus Feb 19; KURS Apr 14, 2026, calling himself 'in a critical minority'). The July crisis (Fedorov fired, 5+ days of protests, Syrskyi removed Jul 21) and a UP report of a Zelensky-Zaluzhnyi talk about an 'election window' raise the odds of a new figure being credited. Fedorov added as a newly popular rival.

Change Research (Jul 9-11) has Vindman 34-24 with 41% undecided. Vindman has raised $16.7M vs Nixon's ~$625K. Nixon edged a tiny Seminole Hob Nob straw poll (31-29), polls slightly better vs Moody (UNF, Jul 20), and progressive insurgents have been winning 2026 Democratic primaries.

Germany indicted Serhii K. (Kuznietsov) in Hamburg on Jul 2. There are no reports of other suspects being located. The remaining suspects are believed to be in Ukraine, which denies involvement, and Poland refused to extradite Zhuravlov in Oct 2025. A new arrest in a specific month is unlikely, though summer travel led to the 2025 arrests.

In the Jun 16 special primary Wahab took 42.8%, Hernandez 16.8% and Israni 12.9%, with Republicans splitting the rest. Hernandez needs near-total consolidation of the other votes. Mail voting began Jul 20, and there is no new polling.

Bonilla remains interim governor. She gave birth Jun 30 but declined maternity leave and governs remotely (Jul 3-7 reports). Sheinbaum refuses to arrest or extradite Rocha (ProPublica Jul 13), and there is no sign he will return from his indefinite leave.

OFAC's Iran actions resumed after the MOU collapsed: Hezbollah finance with the TFTC (Jun 30), Ansari (Jul 10), Shamkhani network (Jul 14) and IRGC procurement (Jul 15). No designation update relabeling a group as an Iranian proxy was found. Low information, so masses were trimmed slightly.

Alcaraz withdrew from Montreal and is on the Cincinnati (Aug 13-23) entry list. Organisers and his team say the comeback is planned there (Jul 16). But as of Jul 20 he was still hitting at low intensity with no sets played and wore a wrist guard on Jul 19. A Cincinnati withdrawal would likely shift the target to the US Open.
